thread:
leo.k: FYI canary surfaced a 403 pattern where org-scoped API keys got routed to pooled workers that treated them as project keys. noticed during spike tests
anika.r: is this limited to requests hitting the pooling layer with project affinity? :thinking:
leo.k: yes, seems routing + worker inference produced mismatch between the token envelope and runtime lookup
aj.patel: that's the legacy dual-prefix shim. worker infers consumer type from key prefix when no explicit claim present
maria.v: tl;dr runtime inference is lossy. we should stop making workers guess if edge can attach a compact claim
sam.s: suggestion: edge does a cheap attest header — origin claim + short sig — so downstream can trust origin without parsing token every time
aj.patel: idea sounds fine, but we must keep hot path perf. the C++ worker checks headers inline for latency reasons
leo.k: proposal: X-Auth-Origin + X-Auth-Attest header where attest is an edge-signed blob (sig, ts, kid). worker verifies signature quickly and uses origin claim
anika.r: example header sketch:
sec-bot: deploy-check: header-schema v1 required for canary
maria.v: ```
X-Auth-Origin: org
X-Auth-Attest: sig=BASE64,kid=edg1,ts=1754340000
```
sam.s: worker pseudocode:
maria.v: ```
if (verify_attest(header.X-Auth-Attest)) {
  origin = header.X-Auth-Origin
} else {
  origin = infer_from_key(key)
}
```
aj.patel: fallback inference only when attest missing. keeps backward compat while making behavior deterministic when present
leo.k: tradeoffs: extra verify cost, key rotation + KMS needs, slightly bigger attack surface if attest scheme flawed
anika.r: ops notes: short TTL on attests, revocation list for edge signing keys, monitoring for failed verify rates
maria.v: RBAC change: when origin==org, prefer org-level RBAC lookup first, then project fallback. update docs and tests
sam.s: tests: canary to force mismatch routing and exercise both verify and infer paths; add metric for origin_mismatch_count
aj.patel: i'll prototype a minimal verify path in C++ worker. aim <200ns without crypto heavy ops (use cached verified keys/kid)
leo.k: action list:
- aj.patel: prototype header verify (P0)
- maria.v: update RBAC lookup order & docs
- anika.r: key rotation + KMS policy + revocation plan
- sam.s: canary harness + telemetry for p95 and verify latency
- leo.k: write RFC follow-up outlining header schema + migration plan
sec-bot: ticket ENGSEC-1824 created: edge-attest-key-rotation-checklist
anika.r: deployment plan: enable attest emission at edge first (no enforcement), roll workers that accept attest, then flip opt-in enforcement for org keys, finally require for all org keys after 2 weeks metrics look good
maria.v: note: need a fallback-mode for inter-region traffic where edge attestation might not be injected yet
sam.s: will add a metric: attest_missing_by_route and origin_inference_mismatch_rate
aj.patel: will try caching kid->pubkey and verify with ed25519 libs; if we hit perf risk we can short-circuit with an allowlist for known-good edges
leo.k: if prototype shows low overhead we schedule a gradual rollout. if we see rising 401/403 we revert edge emit or worker verify flag
anika.r: also update threat model doc: attestation spoof and replay; include nonce/ts and short TTL, and revoke path
maria.v: i'll add a migration checklist in the RBAC doc and record the fallback lookup algorithm explicitly
sam.s: adding canary steps to pipeline and alerts for p95 token auth latency regressions
leo.k: thanks all. i'll consolidate notes into an RFC follow-up and link the PRs
maria.v: closing thread unless new blockers appear, ping here if you see unexpected auth errors after canary
